_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Copy to store/session-efficiency.json and edit for THIS deployment.
store/ is gitignored, so concrete thresholds and label conventions never leave the machine.
Every field is OPTIONAL: a missing file, a missing key, or an out-of-range value falls back
to the built-in default, and the built-in defaults reproduce today's live context-guard
behaviour (src/context-guard.ts:54-55 actPct 0.90 / hardPct 0.97 plus the always-on
pane-saturation net at :53,83). Deleting this file therefore leaves the fleet exactly as it
behaves without P2-B.
saturation: the four P2-B tiers, as fractions of the CALIBRATED per-(agent,model) context
limit (NOT a static 200k -- see context-guard.ts:104-142).
warningPct            -- advisory only, gates nothing.
noNewLargeTaskPct     -- from here up a `large` package is REFUSED. This is the only
behaviour this config can add.
checkpointRequiredPct -- keep equal to the live context-guard actPct unless you are
deliberately re-tuning both; a test asserts the default match.
hardStopPct           -- keep equal to the live context-guard hardPct, same reason.
paneSaturationIsHardStop -- mirror of the always-on net. Only an explicit false disarms it.
taskSizePolicy: DETERMINISTIC size lookup. A kanban label name or card/task type maps to a
size; anything unlisted contributes nothing. There is no pattern inference and NO model call
on this path -- if you want a card treated as large, label it. The shipped default tables are
EMPTY and agentDefault is 'normal', so out of the box nothing is ever refused.
agentDefault -- what an UNMARKED task is treated as. Do NOT set this to 'large' unless you
intend every unlabelled dispatch to be refused into a busy session.
agents: per-agent overrides. A block that omits `saturation` inherits the fleet values above
(not the built-in defaults), so adding a per-agent task-size default cannot silently reset
that agent's thresholds.
